narrative:
The model estimates a 77% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile that strongly signal a higher risk of departure compared to colleagues expected to stay.

Your total years of professional experience stands out as the most influential factor. With 6-10 years overall, you fall into a group that the model associates with greater mobility and openness to new opportunities, unlike the majority of those predicted to stay, who tend to have only 1-5 years of experience.

The second strongest influence is that you have received other job offers while working here. Having external opportunities makes it significantly more likely the model will predict you might leave, as this pattern is far less common among employees expected to remain.

Third, your relatively short tenure in your current role (1-5 years) also pushes the prediction toward leaving. This is typical for many who eventually depart, whereas longer stays in one organization are more common among those the model expects to stay.

Taken together, these elements paint a picture of an experienced professional who is attractive to other employers and has not yet put down deep roots in this organization. The company should consider discussing retention strategies with you, such as faster career progression or enhanced incentives, while you may want to reflect on whether your long-term goals still align with staying.
